title: Quickmart Puts 2 Billion Shares on Sale at KSh7.50 Ahead of NSE Debut
desc: Quickmart has opened its IPO, offering 2 billion shares at KSh7.50 each ahead of its planned November 12 NSE listing.
content:
💼 BUSINESS | 🔵 LATEST

Quickmart Opens KSh15 Billion IPO Ahead of NSE Listing

Excerpt:
Quickmart has opened its IPO, offering 2 billion shares at KSh7.50 each ahead of its planned November 12 NSE listing.

Quickmart has opened its Initial Public Offering (IPO), giving investors an opportunity to buy shares in the Kenyan supermarket chain ahead of its planned listing on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE).

The offer opened at 9:00 a.m. on Monday, October 5, 2026, and will run until 5:00 p.m. on October 30. Quickmart is offering 2 billion existing ordinary shares at KSh7.50 each, representing 50 per cent of the company's issued share capital.

At the offer price, the transaction is targeting about KSh15 billion and gives Quickmart an implied market valuation of approximately KSh30 billion when the shares are listed.

The shares being offered are existing shares held by Sokoni Retail Kenya Limited, meaning the transaction is a sale by an existing shareholder rather than Quickmart issuing new shares to raise fresh capital. Proceeds from the offer will therefore go to the selling shareholder rather than directly into Quickmart's expansion programme.

The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) has approved the offer and its Information Memorandum, while the NSE has approved the admission of Quickmart's entire issued share capital to the Main Investment Market Segment (MIMS).

Quickmart is expected to begin trading on the NSE on November 12, with announcement of the offer results and allocation scheduled for November 6. The company has cautioned that the timetable may change subject to regulatory approval.

The offer has also attracted conditional interest from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), which has committed to purchase offer shares worth up to US$15 million, equivalent to about KSh1.94 billion. The commitment is subject to approval by the IFC Board and does not constitute an endorsement or guarantee of the investment.

Quickmart currently operates 72 stores across 16 counties and says it serves millions of customers through its nationwide retail network. The company reported revenue of KSh50.4 billion in 2025, while its adjusted profit after tax was reported at about KSh1.7 billion.

For Kenyan investors, the opening of the offer marks the start of a significant new opportunity to take an ownership stake in one of the country's major homegrown supermarket chains. Investors should, however, review the official Information Memorandum and applicable risks before making an investment decision.

The offer is scheduled to close on October 30, after which the allocation process will proceed before Quickmart's expected NSE debut in November.
